newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis join rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis join rally.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices rallied sharply on Tuesday in the wake of the latest data on wage inflation, which showed employers' costs were much weaker than anticipated.

This started the market rethinking whether the Federal Reserve would tighten interest rates when its policy-making body next meets on May 20--even though two more important economic reports will be released later this week.

The Employment Cost Index for the first quarter only gained 0.6 percent, confounding predictions that the broad measure of how much it costs companies to employ their workforce, including pay and benefits, would gain 0.9 percent.

"Everyone was fearing the worst and it came out to be very, very positive, so you got a lot of people reassessing the Fed's next meeting," a trader said. "But if you get a bad payrolls (report), it could be right back down," he cautioned.
The Labor Department on Friday is slated to release April payrolls, which economists polled by Reuters forecast would gain 211,000, according to a consensus survey.

But ahead of that important gauge of how successful displaced workers are in finding jobs, the National Association of Purchasing Managment on Wednesday puts out its data that gives traders a look at whether manufacturers are expanding or contracting.
While municipal bond futures outperformed the cash municipal market, as is often the case, traders said that the lag was fairly small, with cash bonds gaining three-quarters to one point.
In the secondary market, Chicago Illinios Board of Education Chicago School Reform of December 2020, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.99 percent NET, down five basis points.

And Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, JFK Internationational Air Terminal LLC Projects of December 2022, which pay a 5.75 percent coupon, were bid at 5.99 percent, NET, down six basis points.
June municipal bond futures rose 1-5/32 to 113-23/32, while June Treasury bonds climbed 1-9/32 to 108-22/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 161 ticks.
